case_name: Robert O. Edwards, Jr. v. Douglas A. Collins
court: United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims

issues.label: NAS reports as constructive record evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether Update 2012 and Update 2010 were constructively part of the record before the AOJ despite not being physically submitted.

issues.label: Direct review docket evidentiary limits under §7113(a)
issues.why: The Board limited its review to evidence of record on the AOJ decision date, and the court must determine whether NAS reports fell within that record.

issues.label: Constructive possession doctrine scope
issues.why: Whether VA's constructive possession of government-generated documents extends to NAS Agent Orange reports affects what the Board must consider.

issues.label: Timing of evidence versus AOJ decision date
issues.why: Update 2012 postdated some events, so the court must resolve whether it existed and was constructively possessed before March 26, 2020.

issues.label: Duty to assist—medical examination trigger
issues.why: The court must decide whether the low threshold of §5103A(d)(2) requiring an exam was met by the biological mechanism theory.

issues.label: Adequacy of Board's reasons or bases
issues.why: Whether the Board sufficiently explained its denial of a medical exam and its treatment of the NAS theory is reviewable.

issues.label: Effect of unrelated Board decisions as evidence
issues.why: The court must assess whether prior Board decisions and their referenced private opinions can indicate a nexus triggering the duty to assist.

issues.label: Non-precedential nature of Board decisions
issues.why: Under 38 C.F.R. §20.1303, prior Board decisions are persuasive only, affecting how much weight Edwards's submissions carry.

issues.label: Whether AOJ failed to consider NAS reports
issues.why: Both AOJ decisions noted no consideration of NAS reports, raising whether required evidence was overlooked.

issues.label: AOJ silence on duty to assist
issues.why: The AOJ did not discuss §5103A, raising whether it failed to fulfill or address its statutory assistance obligation.

issues.label: Distinguishing the April 2015 tongue-cancer decision
issues.why: The Board distinguished it partly by ignoring Update 2010's role, which the court must evaluate.

issues.label: Distinguishing the September 2015 forearm decision
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board properly distinguished a skin-cancer case involving sun exposure.

issues.label: Whether biological mechanism theory indicates nexus
issues.why: The immune-alteration/infection theory's sufficiency to indicate a possible connection is central to the exam-duty question.

issues.label: Direct service connection elements under Washington
issues.why: Edwards must prove the three direct-connection elements since presumptive service connection is unavailable.

issues.label: Non-inclusion in §3.309(e) presumptive list
issues.why: Squamous cell carcinoma's exclusion from presumption shapes the burden and analytical framework.

issues.label: Whether NAS theory counts as argument versus evidence
issues.why: The Board refused to consider Update 2012 as either argument or evidence, which the court must review.

issues.label: Proper remedy—remand scope
issues.why: The court must determine whether remand for exam and NAS consideration is warranted or whether errors are harmless.

issues.label: Correctness of dismissing March 2018 decision
issues.why: Though parties agree it was correctly dismissed, the court should confirm this preliminary determination.

issues.label: Prejudicial versus harmless error analysis
issues.why: Any Board errors must be assessed for prejudice to Edwards's substantial rights.
